decisions.quote: Comparing case vignettes results from two medical schools suggests that reporting explicit demographic diversity was not significantly different. The findings illustrate that sex was the demographic characteristic consistently described, where males were over-represented.
decisions.reason: Although a difference-of-proportions test showed a higher percentage of vignettes specifying race at UNC than at UMN (23.4% vs. 3.3%), race and ethnicity remained overwhelmingly unspecified at both institutions (76.6% and 86.3% unspecified at UNC vs. 96.7% and 98.7% at UMN), sexual orientation was unspecified in over 99% of cases at both schools, and sex was the only demographic characteristic consistently reported in at least half of vignettes, with males over-represented at both schools. In both the Abstract and Discussion, the authors state an overall verdict that reporting explicit demographic diversity (including race and ethnicity) was not distinctly or significantly different from the original UMN study conducted 20 years earlier. Under Rule 1 of the codebook, the authors' overall verdict governs and supports 'successful'.
